clue.text: Builder's joiner is fired ?

definitions.meaning: the paste a bricklayer spreads to bind bricks together
a short-barrelled gun that lobs shells is something fired

explanation.surface: A carpenter on a building site has just been sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joiner' suggests a carpenter and 'fired' a sacking; really the joiner is the paste between bricks, and the second sense is the gun that is fired.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word names the lime-and-sand paste binding brickwork and a stubby artillery piece that is fired at a high angle.

clue.text: Main variety of canoe?

indicators.note: a variety of the word canoe is a different arrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: Someone asks if a certain canoe is a common type.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main' looks like 'chief'; it is the old poetic word for the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The main is a poetic term for the open sea.

clue.text: Someone going to take orders ?

parts.note: suggests a novice entering holy orders, but means a salesman on the road collecting customers' orders

explanation.surface: Someone is about to be ordained as a priest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take orders' suggests becoming a priest; it is the commercial salesman who travels about taking customers' orders.
explanation.definitionFit: A commercial traveller journeys round a district getting orders from shops.

clue.text: Argue about a member of the family

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a son is a member of a family

explanation.surface: Two people quarrel over one of their relatives.
explanation.definitionFit: To reason is to argue a case logically.

clue.text: Is his a spectacular career?

parts.note: 'spectacular' is read as 'to do with spectacles', so the career is that of someone who tests eyes and supplies glasses

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a man's working life has been dazzling.
explanation.definitionFit: This professional prescribes and fits spectacles, so the work is literally about spectacles.

clue.text: Writer drives light loom for manufacturers

indicators.note: the words are raw material for manufacturers, who will make them into something new, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A textile engineer powers a lightweight loom for factory owners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manufacturers' turns DRIVESLIGHTLOOM into the Irish author of The Vicar of Wakefield.
explanation.definitionFit: Oliver Goldsmith was an 18th-century Irish novelist, poet and playwright.

clue.text: Rule about people in building

indicators.note: about means the word for rule goes round the people

parts.note: a tenet is a principle or rule held
men are people

explanation.surface: A regulation concerning who may be inside a building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' places TENET round MEN, splitting it as TENE...T.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenement is a large building divided into flats for rent.

clue.text: Might be treated as containers?

explanation.surface: Some vessels could undergo treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: To a doctor, patients are 'cases', so 'Might be treated' is the first sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor's patients are called cases, and boxes or holders are also cases.

clue.text: Every other treat Neal arranged

indicators.note: arranged means the letters of the two words are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Neal sets up a treat for every other person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' rearranges TREATNEAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Alternate means every second one, as in alternate days.

clue.text: Making amends for getting ready but not starting

indicators.note: not starting means the opening letter of the word for getting ready is dropped

parts.note: the act of getting ready is preparation

explanation.surface: Someone is getting ready to apologise but never quite begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not starting' removes the P from PREPARATION.
explanation.definitionFit: Reparation is compensation given to put right a wrong, the act of making amends.

clue.text: Declines to appear in lots of games

definitions.meaning: goes down, as the sun does in the evening
in tennis a set is a group of games, so several of them are lots of games

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to turn up for a busy sporting programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Declines' looks like 'refuses'; it is the verb for the sun going down.
explanation.definitionFit: The sun sinks below the horizon each evening, and a tennis match is divided into groups of games of that name.

clue.text: Animal is the mount backed to run

indicators.note: backed means the name of the mountain is read from end to start

parts.note: Etna is the famous volcano in Sicily, a mountain
to lope is to run with long easy strides

explanation.surface: A creature is the steed someone has bet on in a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' turns ETNA into ANTE; the surface wants 'backed' as a bet on a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: An antelope is a swift, horned grazing beast of Africa and Asia.

clue.text: Declaration is made in pool

indicators.note: in means the word is sits inside the word for pool

parts.note: a mere is a small lake or pond

explanation.surface: An announcement is made at the swimming baths.
explanation.walkthrough: MISERE is a bid in solo whist undertaking to win no tricks; 'made' just links IS to its container.
explanation.definitionFit: In card games such as solo whist, misère is a bid announcing that the player will lose every trick.

clue.text: Stone work all unfinished

parts.note: op is the short form of opus, a musical work

indicators.note: unfinished means the final letter of the word all is cut off

explanation.surface: Building work on a stone house is left incomplete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfinished' drops the last L of ALL to give AL.
explanation.definitionFit: An opal is a gemstone with shifting rainbow colours.

clue.text: Churchman appears before church-possibly not right

parts.note: pre is the prefix meaning before
CE is the abbreviation for the Church of England

indicators.note: possibly means the letters may be rearranged into another order

explanation.surface: A clergyman turns up ahead of church, possibly not correctly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges NOT + R into NTOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A precentor is the cleric who leads the singing in a cathedral or church.

clue.text: Left in the hunt

parts.note: the cry raised in fox hunting when the quarry has broken cover and departed

explanation.surface: Someone was left behind while the hunt rode on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' reads as 'remaining'; it means 'departed', the hunting cry for a fox that has broken cover.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the huntsman's call that the fox has gone off, and in plain speech means departed.

clue.text: Flier of the new era is to work passage

indicators.note: new means the letters of era come out freshly arranged

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
a lane is a narrow passage

explanation.surface: A pilot of the modern age is going to work his way through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges ERA into AER.
explanation.definitionFit: An aeroplane is a winged aircraft, something that flies.

clue.text: There's one in eight but two in seven

definitions.text: There's one in eight but two in seven

parts.words: There's one in eight but two in seven
parts.note: counts the spoken units of sound in the words 'eight' and 'seven', not anything in the numbers

explanation.surface: A puzzling statement about counting within numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: The numbers look like quantities; it is the words 'eight' (one beat) and 'seven' (two beats).
explanation.definitionFit: A unit of pronunciation; 'eight' has one, 'seven' has two.

clue.text: Giving away carrier breaking the odd bale

indicators.note: breaking means the carrier goes into the middle of the other letters
odd means the letters of bale are made strange, rearranged

parts.note: a tray is something for carrying dishes

explanation.surface: A porter is giving away an odd bundle of hay he carried.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd' rearranges BALE as BE...AL, and 'breaking' puts TRAY between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Betrayal is treachery, such as giving away a secret or a friend to an enemy.

clue.text: Right to fish in the angler's property?

parts.note: an eel is a snake-like fish

explanation.surface: A legal right to fish in a stretch of water belongs to an angler.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests fishing rights; the definition is the angler's reel, his own possession.
explanation.definitionFit: A reel is the spool holding an angler's line, a piece of his own kit.

clue.text: Hurt going round the foreign part of New York

indicators.note: going round means the word for hurt surrounds the foreign word

parts.note: harm is hurt
le is French for the

explanation.surface: An injury occurs when going about the foreign parts of New York.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going round' places HARM around LE, the French 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: Harlem is a district of upper Manhattan, New York City.

clue.text: Book for the simple student?

parts.note: 'simples' is an old word for medicinal plants, so the student of simples needs a book about plants

explanation.surface: A textbook for a slow learner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'simple' looks like 'unintelligent'; in old usage a simple is a medicinal plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A herbal is a book describing plants and their healing uses, the simples of old medicine.

clue.text: Fish is a ray? About right

indicators.note: about means the word for ray goes around the letter for right

parts.note: a beam is a ray of light

explanation.surface: Someone asks if a fish is a ray, and is told that's roughly correct.
explanation.walkthrough: A ray is a fish, which is the false path; here it is a beam of light. 'About' puts BEAM round R.
explanation.definitionFit: Bream is a deep-bodied freshwater or sea fish.

clue.text: Odd phrase in a way — means "hungry"

indicators.note: in means the reworked letters go inside the abbreviation for the way

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

indicators.note: odd means the letters of phrase are made strange, rearranged

explanation.surface: A strange expression in a manner of speaking turns out to mean hungry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odd' rearranges PHRASE into HARPSE, which 'in' places inside ST.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharp-set is an old expression for being ravenous, keen for food.

clue.text: Run for a paper?

parts.note: a run here is both a cricket score not off the bat and a special printing of a newspaper

explanation.surface: Someone dashes out to buy a newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run' suggests a dash to the shop; in cricket a run given away by byes or wides gets this name, as does a special edition of a newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A special late edition of a newspaper is so called, as is a run scored not off the bat in cricket.

clue.text: Some nasty excrescence or sore

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A growth on the skin that is ugly or painful.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition 'or sore' took in the link word 'or'; the definition is 'sore' alone. 'Some' takes STYE from nasTY Excrescence.
explanation.definitionFit: A stye is an inflamed swelling on the eyelid, a small sore.

clue.text: Stones where a fish is swallowing an insect

parts.note: brill is a flatfish

indicators.note: swallowing means the insect goes inside the fish and is

parts.note: an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: A fish is gulping down a bug at the waterside stones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swallowing' puts ANT inside BRILL+IS, between the I and the S.
explanation.definitionFit: Brilliants are diamonds or other gems cut with many facets to sparkle.

clue.text: Ancient monument poor Mr Cole presented to church

indicators.note: poor means the letters of the name are in a bad state, rearranged

explanation.surface: An old memorial to a poor man named Cole was given to the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' rearranges MRCOLE into CROMLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A cromlech is a prehistoric tomb of standing stones topped by a flat capstone.

clue.text: Mother returns without Ena-she's in a frenzy

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the reversed mother wraps the name
returns means the word for mother is read backwards

parts.note: a dam is the mother of an animal
taken as written

explanation.surface: A mother comes home without her daughter Ena, and Ena is frantic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns DAM into MAD, and 'without' (meaning outside) puts it round ENA.
explanation.definitionFit: A maenad was a frenzied female follower of Bacchus, so a woman in a frenzy.
